messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Memory allocation with multithreading
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,

Just to give feedback... I solved my problem on Christmas day haha
Since I don't have much RAM available at the server, my solution was to write a bash file saying that for each model a new process should begin.

In this way, I could parallelize the model (using 28 threads) without caring about a memory burning.
The bash file is quite simple

#!/bin/bash

for i in {1..250}
do
  echo 'R CMD BATCH -$i model22.R'
  R CMD BATCH -$i model22.R
done

These particular 250 models took 7 days to run.

H

Em quarta-feira, 23 de dezembro de 2020 às 16:35:16 UTC-3, Henrique Laureano escreveu:
> Yeah, I'll do that. Tks!
>
> ... What I don't get here is:
> I can run a single model "obj <- MakeADFun() ; opt <- mlminb()" using less than 3G, but when I put that in a loop
> for (i in 1:5) {
>       obj <- MakeADFun()
>       opt <- nlminb()
>       FreeADFun()
>       gc()
> }
> all my memory isn't enough. Since I'm not doing anything new, the memory usage should not be the same?
>
> Another thing...
> I'm used to do loops in parallel (package future, e.g.), but here this should be a bad choice since the model is also in parallel.
> However, this brings me to a new question:
> What should be better here, parallelize the model or parallelize the loop?
>
> H
> Em quarta-feira, 23 de dezembro de 2020 às 14:33:30 UTC-3, fiee...@gmail.com escreveu:
> > I think there are way too many number of threads given your restricted memory; 10Gb is smaller than a laptop. Could you try reducing to 1 core and see how much memory does it take to run your model and then scale up accordingly?
> > K

> > > ﻿Yes, I was using the CRAN version. I tried now with the GitHub one and at the same point, my process got killed.
> > > Before was always a MakeADFUn -> retape memory error, now was just 'killed'.
> > >
> > > Since my models are big (60K data points, 30K groups, 4 latent effects per group), I think there isn't so much more that I can do (Iḿ not doing the AD tape in parallel and I'm using FreeADFun() and gc()) with 10G of RAM.
> > >
> > > H
> > > Em terça-feira, 22 de dezembro de 2020 às 19:29:26 UTC-3, Kasper Kristensen escreveu:
> > > > If you are using the CRAN version of TMB can you try the GitHub version instead? (With recompiled model DLLs).
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Sent from my Huawei Mobile
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > -------- Original Message --------
> > > > Subject: [TMB users] Memory allocation with multithreading
> > > > From: Henrique Laureano
> > > > To: TMB Users
> > > > CC:
> > > >
> > > > Hi guys,
> > > >
> > > > I'm trying to do a simulation study in a server (30 threads and 197G of RAM - however, I can only use 10G. Yes, that's sad).
> > > > To get an idea of the simulation size:
> > > > I generate 5 data samples (I want 1K, but I'm starting with just five), each sample consists of 30K groups of size two (so, 60K data points). with four latent effects per group.
> > > >
> > > > The model is a GLMM, and to get some good initial guesses I fit first a GLM.
> > > > I attached the script, but the idea of what I'm doing is basically
> > > >
> > > > openmp(28) ## I'm using 28 threads. Yes, both models are in parallel
> > > > dyn.load(dynlib('GLM'))
> > > > config(tape.parallel=FALSE, DLL='GLM')
> > > > dyn.load(dynlib('GLMM'))
> > > > config(tape.parallel=FALSE, DLL='GLMM')
> > > > for (i in 1:5) {
> > > >       ## first the GLM
> > > >       objF <- MakeADFun(DLL='GLM')
> > > >       optF <- nlminb()
> > > >       FreeADFun(objF)
> > > >       gc()
> > > >       ## now the GLMM
> > > >       obj <- MakeADFun(DLL='GLMM')
> > > >       opt <- nlmimb()
> > > >       FreeADFun(obj)
> > > >       gc()
> > > > }
> > > > save.image()
> > > >
> > > > Until now, the max I was able to do was to fit three models. Then, I got a problem with memory allocation in the call MakeADFun -> retape.
> > > > I'm already not doing the AD tape in parallel and I'm using both FreeADFun() and gc().
> > > >
> > > > There is something else that I can do to try to keep less stuff in the memory?
> > > > OR, I'm doing something wrong?
> > > >
> > > > Since I have to always generate new data and fit a GLM for the initial guesses, I don't see any smart way instead of working with two DLL at the same script.
> > > >
> > > > The complete script follows attached.
> > > > Since now, tks for any help!
> > > >
> > > > Best,
> > > > H
